transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-01-22 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alice Reed (Redwood AE), Carlos Vega (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Rivermark CTO), Mark Ellis (Rivermark Head of Security), Janelle Wu (Rivermark Compliance), Tom Alvarez (Rivermark Platform)

Summary: Brief intro, qualification, detailed questions about data residency (EU, UK), HIPAA applicability for loan origination docs, logging constraints (no full-text logs for PII), KMS integration, SOC2/ISO documents. Next steps agreed: security pack, technical deep dive + benchmarks, pricing for Dedicated pilot.

[00:00] Alice: Hey everyone thanks for making time, I'm Alice Reed from Redwood, i'll kick us off, Carlos from our solutions team will cover the technical side. Quick round robin?
[00:12] Priya: Priya here, CTO at Rivermark. We're evaluating LLM features for customer support automation and some internal document summarization, worried about residency and regs.
[00:20] Mark: Mark Ellis, head of security. We'll be the gating on any hosted data flows.
[00:24] Janelle: Janelle, compliance. We'll need to map to GDPR and a couple of HIPAA-adjacent flows.
[00:29] Alice: Great thanks. Carlos, over to you for a quick product framing.
[00:33] Carlos: Thanks Alice. Redwood offers hosted API, reserved Dedicated pools, and a Private deployment option for VPC/on-prem. For many banks we do Dedicated first — predictable throughput and isolation — then move to Private where needed. We'll go through how data flows and controls map to residency and compliance.
[00:50] Priya: Quick question — how strict is your hosted offering on data leaving regions? Our EU customers need EU-only processing for some products.
[00:58] Carlos: Good Q. Hosted supports region pinning for processing — EU regions, UK, US — but the standard hosted logs/store metadata may still route through Redwood control plane for ops unless you choose Dedicated or Private. For strict EU-only agreements we recommend Dedicated with regional capacity or Private VPC so control plane endpoints remain in your VPC.
[01:20] Mark: When you say "control plane", does that mean metadata like request headers and user IDs could leave the region?
[01:26] Carlos: By default yes some operational metadata may be present for telemetry, error reporting; we can scope that via contractual terms and opt-outs. In Dedicated we can restrict telemetry flow and in Private it's customer-managed. Also we offer redaction hooks to strip PII before logs.
[01:41] Janelle: For GDPR we need the ability to delete customer personal data on demand and a data processing addendum. Do you support DSAR workflows?
[01:49] Alice: Yes, we have a standard DPA and DSAR processes. For Hosted customers we handle deletion requests, but for Dedicated/Private you get more control to implement retention policies. We'll send our DPA in the security pack.
[02:05] Priya: HIPAA — not all our workloads are PHI, but loan origination and some health-benefit products might contain PHI. Can you support a BAA?
[02:15] Alice: Redwood has a BAA offering for Dedicated and Private deployments — Hosted customers can qualify case-by-case; typically we prefer Dedicated/Private for BAA due to isolation and audit requirements.
[02:26] Tom: Operationally we can't have full-text logs of customer PII in S3 for more than 30 days, and in some EU jurisdictions 0 days retention. Can Redwood provide redaction at ingestion?
[02:35] Carlos: We have pre-ingest redaction and tokenization helpers — regex and model-assisted PII stripping. For strict no-storage, we can enable transient processing with no persistent logs; need to align on SLA tradeoffs because that affects incident investigation capability.
[02:50] Priya: What about KMS/HSM? We require customer-managed keys for at-rest data encryption for Dedicated.
[02:58] Carlos: Dedicated supports BYOK (bring your own key) via major KMS providers and HSM options in Private deployments. We also support envelope encryption so model weights remain encrypted and per-tenant data tokens are under your KMS.
[03:12] Mark: Auditability — we need immutable audit logs for admin actions and model version rollouts for at least 5 years.
[03:19] Alice: Our Console includes audit trails. For Dedicated we can store immutable audit logs in your account or ship them to your SIEM. 5 years is a long retention; that's an add-on but possible. We'll include retention options in the pack.
[03:34] Janelle: Any certifications — SOC2, ISO27001?
[03:37] Alice: Yes SOC2 Type II; ISO for select deployments. We'll include copies of our attestations and the pen test summary.
[03:45] Priya: Technically, Carlos, if we do Dedicated, can we run some internal models and not expose data to Redwood's model catalog? We want to restrict model variants.
[03:55] Carlos: You can pin model versions and disable automatic fallbacks. In Dedicated we can also limit the available model catalog to curated ones and prevent fallback to hosted variants. Private gives you full control.
[04:08] Tom: We have throughput peaks during statement season, need autoscale and burst. How does Dedicated handle burst to other regions?
[04:16] Carlos: Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling and cross-region burst. We can set policies to favor local capacity and fallback to other regions as a last resort; cross-region falls under residency constraints though so we'd need exceptions documented.
[04:32] Priya: On logging, we need the ability to completely disable request/response retention for certain routes — e.g., SSN extraction pipeline. Is route-level retention config supported?
[04:44] Carlos: Yes route-level policies in the Console allow per-route retention and redaction rules. For stricter needs we can implement server-side suppression so responses are never persisted. That said, that limits debugging.
[04:59] Mark: Data breach notification — what's your SLA for notifying customers? 72 hours?
[05:04] Alice: We follow standard incident response with 72-hour notification for reportable breaches; for Dedicated/Private customers we also provide runbooks and direct channels.
[05:14] Janelle: For GDPR, transfer mechanisms, do you support SCCs?
[05:18] Alice: We support SCCs and in our DPA. For on-prem or EU Dedicated, transfers are minimized.
[05:26] Priya: Let's talk about redaction imperfections — the regex approach misses things. Do you have model-assisted PII detectors run before logging?
[05:34] Carlos: Yes we have a hybrid pipeline — regex + ML detectors + deterministic tokenization. We can surface confidence scores and flag uncertain items for review rather than logging raw text.
[05:45] Tom: For benchmarks — we want latency under 150ms p50 for short prompts, and cost targets. Can you run a benchmark with our sample workload?
[05:54] Carlos: Absolutely. We'll need a test harness, sample prompts, and a preferred model. For a Dedicated pilot we can run on a reserved pool and provide metrics (p50/p95/p99, throughput, cost per 1k tokens). I'll coordinate with your ops team.
[06:09] Priya: Any limitations on model calling to downstream tools — i.e., storing tool call logs? Those calls might contain account numbers.
[06:17] Carlos: Tool calls can be instrumented and we can redact tool payloads server-side. Also you can configure so that tool call traces are never persisted.
[06:26] Mark: Are there any third-party subprocessors we should be aware of? For example, do you use any external logging or analytics vendors that might touch customer data?
[06:34] Alice: We list subprocessors in the DPA — common ones are cloud providers for infra (AWS, GCP), monitoring services, and CDN for static assets; we can provide a current list. For Dedicated/Private we can reduce or eliminate some subprocessors.
[06:47] Janelle: Regarding PHI, if we sign a BAA, do you allow a Dedicated deployment with customer-managed keys and on-prem control plane?
[06:57] Alice: Yes that's our recommended path for PHI-heavy workloads. Private deployments can be fully customer-managed with HSM and no Redwood-managed control plane connectivity if needed.
[07:08] Priya: What's the typical timeline to stand up a Dedicated pilot?
[07:12] Alice: Usually 4-6 weeks — provisioning, network setup (VPC peering / PrivateLink), model pinning, and security review. Private on-prem can take longer.
[07:22] Tom: Network — do you support AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering?
[07:26] Carlos: We support PrivateLink and VPC peering and have documentation for both. We'll need an IP allowlist and firewall rules; we can share the exact ports.
[07:37] Mark: Encryption in transit: mutual TLS?
[07:40] Carlos: Mutual TLS is supported for Dedicated and Private endpoints, yes.
[07:44] Alice: Quick qualification: what's your timeline and decision process?
[07:49] Priya: We're aiming to pick a vendor by end of Q1, pilot in Q2, go-live for first set of features Q3. Security and compliance need to sign off. Budget's allocated but we need firm pricing.
[08:02] Alice: Good — that aligns with our typical ramp. We'll get you pricing for a 3-month Dedicated pilot and the security pack.
[08:10] Janelle: Do you support data residency constraints per tenant — like UK-only for product A and US-only for product B?
[08:17] Carlos: Yes, request routing policies let you pin models/requests to regions at tenant or route level. It requires capacity planning per region for Dedicated.
[08:27] Priya: We also have concerns about model updates — we need to lock model versions and have canary rollouts.
[08:34] Carlos: Console supports model pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallbacks. For Dedicated we can do manual approval gates.
[08:44] Tom: How do you handle backups — are they encrypted with customer keys?
[08:48] Carlos: Backups can be encrypted with customer KMS keys in Dedicated/Private. For Hosted, backups are Redwood-managed but encrypted — we can negotiate custody for enterprise deals.
[08:58] Mark: Any limitations on number of audit log exports or integration with Splunk/Datadog?
[09:03] Alice: We integrate with Splunk/Datadog/S3 exports and can set scheduled exports for long-term retention. There may be costs for storage/ingress.
[09:12] Priya: Can we get a stub of the network diagram and control plane architecture?
[09:17] Alice: Yes we'll include a high-level network diagram in the pack and we can schedule an architecture deep dive.
[09:25] Janelle: A question about legal holds — sometimes regulators ask us to freeze deletion. Can you flex retention?
[09:31] Carlos: We can implement legal hold states for data so deletion requests are deferred. That's easier in Dedicated/Private.
[09:39] Priya: Ok let's talk blockers — what's the main risk if we choose Hosted?
[09:44] Alice: Residual telemetry and control plane metadata, potential cross-region metadata routing, and less contractual control around subprocessors. For strict residency/HIPAA we recommend Dedicated or Private.
[09:58] Mark: For Dedicated pricing, do you do committed monthly or annual?
[10:02] Alice: Both — committed monthly/annual. We'll include example TCO for annual commit vs on-demand.
[10:10] Tom: For the test harness, we'll need SSH keys and an ephemeral dataset with masked IDs.
[10:15] Carlos: Understood, we'll coordinate offline.
[10:19] Priya: Any references with other banks who've done similar?
[10:23] Alice: We can share anonymized case studies and reference contacts — many regional banks are on Dedicated with similar controls.
[10:30] Janelle: For DSARs, how do you prove deletion across caches and backups?
[10:36] Carlos: We have deletion workflows and can provide attestations; for Dedicated you control backups so it's straightforward. For Hosted we provide deletion logs and can assist in audits.
[10:48] Alice: Quick pause — anything else we should cover before the next steps?
[10:52] Mark: One last — are test environments isolated from prod?
[10:56] Carlos: Yes test environments can be isolated with separate keys and separate Dedicated pools.
[11:02] Priya: Great. Can we recap next steps?
[11:06] Alice: Sure — I'll send the security pack (SOC2, DPA, BAA sample, subprocessors list, network diagram) by Monday 2026-01-25. Carlos will schedule the technical deep dive and benchmarking the week of 2026-02-02 and will need sample prompts and SSH details. We'll also provide Dedicated pilot pricing by 2026-01-27. Priya to share list of products/workloads and residency map by 2026-01-29.
[11:31] Tom: sounds good.
[11:33] Janelle: Thanks everyone.
[11:35] Alice: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

Note: Transcription includes a few overlaps and minor mis-hearings, e.g., "control plane" occasionally transcribed as "control plain", "KMS" sometimes as "K-M-S".
